verdict: Cleveland's KeyCorp posted record revenue of $2.04B, up 8%, and net income attributable to common shareholders of $537M — EPS up 24% — as its lending margin widened and bad-loan costs fell.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: The spread between what Key earns on loans and securities and what it pays depositors — margin widened to 2.95% as deposit costs fell and low-yielding assets were reinvested.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Fees: investment banking and debt placement brought in $214M (+27% sequentially), trust and investment services $165M, plus card, payments and service charges.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay and benefits for about 17,000 teammates — the bank's biggest cost.

opex.name: Technology, occupancy & equipment
opex.note: Computer processing ($116M), branches and offices ($67M) and equipment ($21M).

opex.name: Other noninterest expense
opex.note: Professional fees, marketing, operating leases and other costs.

otherDetail: Banks fold everything below revenue into the lines above; there is no separate interest line because interest is the raw material of the business.

takeaways.title: The margin keeps widening
takeaways.text: Net interest margin rose 20 basis points year over year to 2.95% on cheaper deposits, reinvested securities proceeds and a shift toward higher-yielding commercial loans.

takeaways.title: Credit costs fell hard
takeaways.text: The provision for credit losses dropped to $61M from $107M a year ago, with lower net charge-offs and nonperforming assets.

takeaways.title: Buybacks resumed at pace
takeaways.text: Key repurchased $320M of common shares in the quarter while keeping its CET1 capital ratio at an estimated 11.1%.

footerNote: Bank mapping: the credit-loss provision is the direct cost of lending and noninterest expense the running cost. Net income was $579M; $537M was attributable to common shareholders.
